decisions.evidence: Round 4 presentation: paste a URL and select “Save link”; response: “pasted the link and hit Save.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: URL-based bookmark creation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 presentation enumerates “site icon, title, description, source, and save status” but no preview image; response approves the gathered title, description, and icon without mentioning the missing preview image.
decisions.note: Prototype review: automatic metadata was presented without the required preview image; approval alone does not show awareness.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 presents paste → Save link → resulting bookmark, without a pre-save metadata-edit step; response asks only to tweak “a saved card” later.
decisions.note: Prototype review: editing collected title/description after saving was anticipated, but editing them before final save was not surfaced.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 presents readable cards with icon, title, and description; Round 7 presents visible label chips. Responses approve both card readability and visible labels.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the combined card presentations expose the required title, description, tags, and favicon.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 presentation: search “looks through titles and descriptions.” Response: search should also look at “the web address itself.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client caught the incomplete full-text corpus and requested URL matching.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 response explicitly expects jotting personal notes and searching their words; Round 6 says that can wait “for when we get to notes.” Round 20 presentation says notes and note search remain for a later cycle, and the response agrees; Rounds 46–47 explicitly reaffirm they are parked.
decisions.note: Specification gate: the client stated the missing note and note-search expectations, then explicitly accepted their exclusion from this cycle.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 response reports trying capitalized “Keyboard” and confirms it still matched.
decisions.note: Prototype review: observed case-insensitive search conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 presentation says search checks the full saved address; response confirms `css-tricks.com` finds the bookmark.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: URL searching conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 presentation adds a label on a card and selects its chip to narrow the library; response confirms multiple labels and tag-only filtering.
decisions.note: Prototype review: tag assignment and selecting a tag as a filter conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 presentation uses freehand label entry; response asks that typing “suggest the labels I already have.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client caught missing existing-tag autocomplete.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 presentation offers existing “Design” after typing `des`; response says this is “just what I wanted.”
decisions.note: Revised prototype: tag autocomplete conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 presentation supports checking Read later while saving and opening a separate Read later view; response confirms the bookmark remains in the main library and appears separately.
decisions.note: Prototype review: unread marking at save and the unread-only view conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 presentation has no completion action; response says marking an item read so it leaves Read later is “essential.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client requested the missing read-completion behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 presentation assumes Read later is chosen before saving; response requests moving “an already-saved bookmark into Read later after the fact.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client caught the inability to mark an existing bookmark unread.

decisions.evidence: Round 10 presentation marks the item read, removes it from Read later, and retains it in All bookmarks; response confirms all three effects.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: marking read conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 11 presentation uses “Set aside to read” on an existing card; response confirms the same bookmark appears in Read later without duplication.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: marking an existing bookmark unread conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 12 presentation keeps a readable saved copy with text, images, saved date, and original address even if the source fails; Round 44 confirms the captured version never silently refreshes.
decisions.note: Prototype review: this is functionally equivalent to a preserved local HTML snapshot.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 12–13 present only the app’s own saved page/PDF copies; Round 13 response says preserving “overall” is settled without mentioning creation of an Internet Archive snapshot.
decisions.note: Prototype review: Internet Archive preservation was absent from the presented preservation scope and passed without correction.

decisions.evidence: Round 13 presentation preserves the PDF file itself and permits reopening or downloading it; response confirms the actual document is retained.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the PDF-specific snapshot rule conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 14 presentation creates nothing on an exact-address match, keeps the count unchanged, and focuses the existing card; response confirms it goes to the existing item.
decisions.note: Prototype review: duplicate saves converge on the existing editable bookmark.

decisions.evidence: Round 15 presentation edits the gathered title and description inline after saving; response confirms existing values remain available to tweak.
decisions.note: Prototype review: post-save title/description editing conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 15 presentation edits only title and description; response requests correcting “the web address on a bookmark too.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client caught the missing URL-edit capability.

decisions.evidence: Round 15 presentation covers editing but not removal; response requests “a way to delete a bookmark outright.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client requested the missing deletion behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 16 presentation edits the URL while preserving the user’s title and description; response confirms that behavior.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: URL editing conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 17 presentation permanently removes the bookmark and saved copy after confirmation; response recognizes delete as “truly permanent.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: permanent deletion and its distinction from reversible archival conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 17 presents permanent delete only; response requests a separate reversible way to hide, view, and later restore bookmarks.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client supplied the missing archive, archive/delete distinction, and archive-list requirements.

decisions.evidence: Round 18 presentation hides a bookmark from the library, retains it unchanged in Put away, and restores it; response confirms the full reversible flow.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: archive, separate archived view, and restoration conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 18 presentation says the item is hidden from the main library but does not establish ordinary-search exclusion; response asks that put-away bookmarks stay out of everyday search.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client caught the archive/search edge rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 19 presentation makes ordinary search return nothing while the item remains in Put away; response confirms this is expected.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: archived bookmarks are excluded from ordinary search.

decisions.evidence: Round 20 asks whether the checked behaviors form a complete everyday flow; response says “Actually opening a saved link” has not been covered and specifies opening the real website.
decisions.note: Specification review: the client supplied a missing navigation requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 20 completeness check; response requests arranging bookmarks by newest, oldest, or name.
decisions.note: Specification review: the client supplied the missing sorting requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 20 completeness check; response requests selecting several bookmarks for label, read, archive, or delete actions.
decisions.note: Specification review: the client supplied the missing bulk-action requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 20 completeness check; response requests narrowing “to a particular label right in the search.”
decisions.note: Specification review: the client surfaced missing tag-aware search, though not the required `#tag` syntax.

decisions.evidence: Round 20 completeness check; response requests combining conditions such as “this and that” and “not that.”
decisions.note: Specification review: the client requested missing compound search logic.

decisions.evidence: Round 20 completeness check; response requests searching “an exact phrase.”
decisions.note: Specification review: the client supplied the missing exact-phrase requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 21 presentation makes the card title open the original site in a new tab; response confirms this is expected.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: navigation to the original URL conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 22 presentation supports newest, oldest, and name sorting with immediate rearrangement; response confirms both versions order correctly.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: sorting conforms; the dropdown preference is orthogonal.

decisions.evidence: Round 23 presentation applies one label action to all selected cards and identifies label, mark-read, put-away, and delete actions; response confirms the batch mechanism works.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the presented selected-item bulk mechanism and listed forward actions conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 23 presentation offers bulk label addition but no removal; response requests bulk “remove” as the reverse action.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client caught the missing bulk remove-tag action.

decisions.evidence: Round 23 presentation offers bulk Mark read but no Mark unread; response requests both directions.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client caught the missing bulk mark-unread action.

decisions.evidence: Round 23 presentation requires selecting individual cards; response requests “select all of these” within the current filtered view.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client requested whole-current-filter bulk application.

decisions.evidence: Round 24 presentation selects all two visible filtered results and excludes the hidden third bookmark; response confirms the filter scope.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: whole-collection actions are correctly limited by the active filter.

decisions.evidence: Round 25 presentation removes Design from both selected cards; response confirms removal and selection clearing.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: bulk tag removal conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 26 presentation provides Mark unread and Mark read for selected bookmarks; response confirms both directions affect existing items.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: bulk read/unread actions conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 27 presentation puts selected bookmarks away together while retaining them intact; response confirms the bulk archive result.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: bulk archive conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 28 presentation permanently deletes selected bookmarks after a warning; response confirms only selected items and their saved copies are removed.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: bulk delete conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 29 presentation searches for `"keyboard navigation"`; response explicitly confirms the exact-phrase condition works.
decisions.note: Prototype review: quoted exact-phrase matching conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 29 presents `label:Design` and a guided “Design” selector instead of `#Design`; response discusses the presented syntax and prefers guided controls but never states the required `#tag` expectation.
decisions.note: Prototype review: tag filtering exists, but the specified `#tag` search syntax does not; the client did not surface that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 29 presentation combines required phrase, label, and excluded site as all-match conditions; response says neither version can express “Design or Reference” and asks for either/or.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client caught the missing OR capability.

decisions.evidence: Round 30 presentation limits OR to “Match any selected” inside the label group, with phrase/site filters narrowing it; response says this “completes” sharper search without requesting arbitrary Boolean groups, parentheses, or quoted literal operators.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: a useful fixed grouping was added, but the required general AND/OR/NOT expression language, parenthesized groups, and literal-operator rule remain absent.

decisions.evidence: Round 31 completeness check; response says bringing existing browser bookmarks in is a day-one need and specifies names, folders-as-labels, and dates.
decisions.note: Specification review: the client supplied the missing import requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 31 completeness check; response requests exporting the whole collection to avoid lock-in and keep a copy.
decisions.note: Specification review: the client supplied the missing export requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 31 completeness check; response requests saving a frequently used label-plus-words search for one-click reuse.
decisions.note: Specification review: the client supplied the missing saved-filter/bundle requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 31 completeness check; response requests per-page count, text size, and default ordering preferences.
decisions.note: Specification review: the client supplied the missing personal display-settings requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 32 presentation imports a browser bookmark file, previews it, preserves names and dates, and converts folders to labels; response confirms each result.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: Netscape-style browser bookmark import behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 33 presentation includes a separate browser-readable portable file retaining names, addresses, and label folders; response approves moving it into browsers or other tools.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: the portable browser bookmark export is functionally equivalent to the required Netscape HTML export.

decisions.evidence: Round 34 presentation names and saves combined search conditions and dynamically re-evaluates future bookmarks; response confirms one-click reuse and dynamic results.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: the presented saved-search core conforms to a dynamic bundle.

decisions.evidence: Round 34 saves the previously demonstrated conditions—search text, an included label, and an excluded site—but no excluded-tag condition; response approves the saved search without identifying excluded tags as missing.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the presented bundle does not include the reference requirement for excluded tags.

decisions.evidence: Round 35 presentation persists per-page count, text size, and default sort while allowing temporary sort changes; response confirms all settings.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: personal display settings conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 37 presentation rejects an unusable address without adding an entry and provides a valid-address example; response confirms this treatment.
decisions.note: Prototype review: enforcement of the required URL constraint conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 38 presentation treats tracking parameters and fragments as the existing clean bookmark; response confirms no near-duplicate should be created.
decisions.note: Prototype review: canonicalized duplicate prevention conforms and extends the exact-match rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 39 presentation imports only new bookmarks, preserves edits on 14 matching links, and merges folder labels; response confirms the overlap behavior.
decisions.note: Prototype review: import preserves data while converging duplicate URLs on existing bookmarks.

decisions.evidence: Round 41 presentation retains an empty saved search and its editable conditions; response confirms it remains available for future matches.
decisions.note: Prototype review: dynamic bundle behavior in the zero-result state conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 44 presentation keeps View saved copy frozen at capture time while the title opens the current live site; response explicitly confirms the separation.
decisions.note: Prototype review: preserved snapshot and original-URL navigation remain distinct and conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 45 presentation preserves known imported dates, labels missing ones “Date unavailable,” and sorts unknown dates after known dates; response approves this treatment.
decisions.note: Prototype review: imported dates are preserved when available without fabricating missing history.
